answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can utilize a Sybil resistance mechanism known as a "mirror identity test". This test requires agents to prove their physical presence at a randomly selected geographic location, such as a distinctive knoll, by capturing and sharing a unique umber-colored QR code displayed on a physical marker. An attacker attempting to create multiple fake identities would need to physically travel to each location, making it costly and impractical to create a large number of Sybil identities, thereby securing the network.
